prospects.thesis: LMT is the highest-scoring prospect and offers scaled exposure to defense primes benefiting from elevated global military budgets, F-35 sustainment, and missile/hypersonics demand. With a modest 1.8x P/S versus peers and bullish options + institutional flows, the stock is participating in the defense rotation while remaining fundamentally reasonable. Recent +19.1% 1M momentum reflects renewed FY26 budget clarity and Middle East/Pacific tailwinds.

AVAV is a pure-play on unmanned systems and loitering munitions (Switchblade), a sub-niche distinct from the large primes and directly tied to Ukraine replenishment and DoD Replicator initiative funding. At $7.7B cap with bullish options and institutional signals, it offers higher-beta drone exposure with a more digestible 1M move (+7.3%) than peers that have already run. Catalyst: continued Switchblade 600 orders and Blue Halo integration synergies.

LDOS provides defense IT/services exposure — a distinct sub-niche from hardware primes — with strong federal digital modernization backlog and healthcare/intel analytics tailwinds. At just 0.8x P/S, it's the cheapest name in the top ranks with bullish options and institutional accumulation. Catalyst: continued civilian and DoD IT contract wins plus margin expansion from the SES portfolio.

SNOW provides essential AI/ML diversification away from the heavy defense tilt, positioned as the enterprise data cloud layer for generative AI workloads (Cortex, Arctic LLM). Bullish options and institutional signals plus a +17% 1M move indicate renewed conviction post-CEO transition and accelerating consumption trends. Catalyst: continued AI-driven data workload monetization and Q2 FY27 print.

KTOS offers unique exposure to tactical jet drones (Valkyrie/CCA program), hypersonic targets, and satellite ground systems — a differentiated sub-niche vs. traditional primes and small drones. The flat 1M performance (-0.2%) while peers ran creates a relative-value setup with bullish options flow suggesting a catch-up trade. Catalyst: USAF Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) production decisions and Space Force ground system awards.

market_pulse.rotation_analysis: Big money is piling into Healthcare right now, and it's not subtle — the options market is betting heavily on XLV moving higher with call volume more than double normal, which lines up with Washington cooling off on the harshest drug pricing rhetoric and the sector looking cheap after a rough stretch of Medicare negotiation headlines and RFK Jr.-driven volatility. On the flip side, Financials are getting hit with genuinely eye-popping bearish bets — a put/call ratio of 6 is the kind of number you see when institutions are seriously worried, likely tied to credit spreads widening, regional bank stress, and the growing sense that "higher for longer" rates plus a softening consumer could crack loan books, especially with tariff-driven inflation keeping the Fed handcuffed. Industrials getting sold is the tell that connects everything: despite all the reshoring and infrastructure spending talk, smart money seems skeptical that tariff policy actually helps domestic manufacturers when it also raises their input costs and invites retaliation. Historically, this exact combo — defensive healthcare bid, financials and cyclicals dumped, credit spreads widening — is a classic late-cycle rotation that precedes an economic slowdown by one to three months. The contradiction worth noting: equity indexes near highs while investment-grade bonds (LQD) show a put/call of 16 is wild — that's institutions screaming that even safe corporate debt is being hedged, which almost never happens in a truly healthy market. The non-obvious read the headlines are missing: everyone's watching tariffs and the Fed, but the real story in this flow is that credit markets are flashing yellow well before stocks are, and when LQD options get this bearish it often means someone big knows a refinancing wall or a specific credit event is coming that hasn't hit the tape yet.
